text: The Compactness Theorem states that a set $T$ of first-order sentences has a model if and only if:
choices: every finite subset of $T$ has a model
explanation: Compactness: $T$ has a model iff every finite subset of $T$ has one. $T$ need not be finite; the theorem's power is precisely for infinite $T$ (e.g. building nonstandard models). Completeness (deciding every sentence) is a different property, and possessing a countable model is the conclusion of Lowenheim-Skolem, not the compactness criterion.
